Description: In Martha Galley’s Master bedroom, John Hobbes questions her about the wedding and family structure, confirms that Martha Galley never truly married, and gains important directional information about the Attic and the piano.
Location: Master bedroom (Master bedroom)
Key Information:
  - The conversation takes place in Martha Galley’s Master bedroom (Master bedroom).
  - Martha Galley asks whether John Hobbes has determined the source of the gunshot; John deliberately downplays the situation and relays Edmund Galley’s claim that "everything is under control."
  - John Hobbes re-confirms the piano as the emergency gathering signal: if someone plays the piano, everyone should go to the Living room (Living room).
  - Martha Galley confirms the villa’s piano was purchased recently, but she can no longer remember why; she only says Edmund Galley likes music.
  - Martha Galley says the piano functioned normally only once last night, and at that time she and Oswald listened to it together.
  - John Hobbes tells Martha Galley that Oswald has been locked into the Kitchen pantry by Edmund Galley.
  - When asked directly about emotions and family structure, Martha Galley clearly states she has always lived alone and has never been married.
  - Martha Galley admits she once held a "wedding-like" celebration and even prepared a dress for it, but it did not correspond to any actual marriage relationship.
  - Martha Galley explicitly denies knowing the identity of Edmund Galley’s father and asks not to be judged for it.
  - Regarding Oswald’s claim that he "remembers Martha Galley’s wedding," Martha Galley clearly says Oswald’s statements should not be believed.
  - John Hobbes recalls that when he first arrived at the villa he was nearly struck by something that fell from upstairs, and asks whether there is a room that can overlook the Entrance (Entrance).
  - Martha Galley directs John Hobbes to check the Attic (Attic), and subjectively believes the incident may have been caused by Oswald, who is locked in the pantry.
  - John Hobbes decides to go investigate the Attic immediately and then leaves the Master bedroom.
Characters:
  [John Hobbes (John Hobbes)] Person No. 1, an outsider investigator.
    · Confirms the gunshot incident with Martha Galley and deliberately calms her emotions.
    · Re-emphasizes the unified rule of using the piano as an emergency gathering signal.
    · Proactively asks about Martha Galley’s marriage and family structure.
    · Questions Oswald’s claim about "Martha Galley’s wedding."
    · Raises key spatial questions about the falling object upstairs and a room that can overlook the Entrance.
    · After obtaining the Attic clue, decides to investigate immediately.
  [Martha Galley (Martha Galley)] Person No. 5, the female owner of the villa.
    · Shows concern about the gunshot and the situation, but visibly relaxes after learning Oswald is restrained.
    · Confirms the piano was purchased recently, but she no longer knows why.
    · Recalls the piano only played normally once last night, and she and Oswald were present.
    · States clearly she has never married, only held a wedding-like celebration once.
    · Denies knowing Edmund Galley’s father’s identity and asks that no judgment be made.
    · Explicitly denies the credibility of Oswald’s claim about her wedding.
    · Directs John Hobbes to the Attic to investigate the source of the falling object above the Entrance.
